headline: Nvidia's next AI accelerator, Rubin, is expected to use mostly 12-layer HBM4 memory, digitimes reports, even though other reports said Nvidia wanted more 8-layer parts.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from 6: only the opening sentence could be read.
importance_line: It affects memory makers Samsung and SK hynix and Nvidia's supply plans for Rubin, though it is a trade-press forecast and the earlier 8-layer reports are unconfirmed.
summary: digitimes reports that most of the memory in Nvidia's coming Rubin AI chips is expected to be 12-layer HBM4, a stacked high-speed memory, even though earlier reports said Nvidia had asked Samsung Electronics and SK hynix for more of the 8-layer kind.
notes: Paywalled; headline and opening sentence only.
